correctness.rationale: The 2025 primary theorem and resolution convention identify sixteen generalized-quadrangle vertices and four mutually disjoint extra vertices meeting four disjoint maximum independent rook-graph sets. The two explicit order-four group Latin squares realize the two classified graph types; their unlike four-coloring counts certify nonisomorphism. Adjacency spectral factorization follows from B^T B=4I and R B=2(J-B), with a 2-by-2 constant block and three paired zero-sum symbol blocks. Weighted intersection matrix factorization uses the -2/-1 curve self-intersections and yields rank 11 and inertia (1,10,9). The coloring proof reduces to a finite sum over all 24^4 choices of four permutation rows, retaining precisely 576 valid Latin squares; a complete frequency table and independent direct backtracking confirm counts 5400 and 8568. CHECK.py reconstructs and tests both polynomials using exact integer Newton identities. All statements are explicitly about these finite objects; no unknown actual realizability is assumed.

value.rationale: The initiating classification poses two natural geometric incidence possibilities for extremal non-K3 quartics with twenty lines, and leaves one realizability alternative open. Counting four-color decompositions of their resolved intersection graphs counts partitions of the candidate line classes into four mutually disjoint curve families. The exact values 225 and 357 distinguish the two possibilities despite completely coincident adjacency and geometric Gram spectra, showing a specific failure of spectral tests to separate these constrained algebraic-geometric configurations. The exact values are not an arbitrary slice: four is the minimum palette forced by each rook row clique, and the two configurations are the entire source-classified list.
